items.title: Norman Simmons interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 27, 2007 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: when I first was with Dakota Staton, I had been with Carmen and everything like that. And with Buster... he said 'I would have brought the whole group up there except they didn’t know no tunes.'

ctx.x: Oh Ron Carter. Oh he was looking for a bass player.

There was no bass player. All over the country, “I can’t find a bass player.” They can play the bass but they don’t know no tunes. They ain’t got — you know what I mean? Same thing Dakota — when Buster Williams, when I first was with Dakota Staton, I had been with Carmen and everything like that. And with Buster, “where did you find this cat?” See I was working down there someplace, Cleveland, someplace in a group and he was down there. He said “I would have brought the whole group up there except they © Fillius…

didn’t know no tunes. The piano player knows no songs.” You know? And that’s what was represented. So now when we come together now they’re interested in our history and now we can all be on the stage together. Because the kids that I work with at William Paterson and the various different schools, now we can all play together. There was a period of time when we couldn’t play together.
